Jordan —

Thanks — reviewed the questions. Quick note up front: we can support both asks, but terms differ depending on whether you want a pure time‑boxed trial (fixed days) or a credit‑bucket pilot (credits allocated over time). Below are two options with pros/cons so procurement can pick which aligns with their accounting model.

Option A — Credit‑Lattice Pilot (recommended for tuning work)
- Structure: 60k token credits delivered as two tranches (30k at kickoff, 30k at T+3w).
- Surge allowance: one conditional burst (additional 15k tokens) that is not invoiced if usage during burst stays below 48 hours and average latency/SLOs unchanged.
- Billing: two invoices aligned with tranches; unused credits expire at pilot end (standard).
- Upside: preserves unit economics for you while letting engineering tune without immediate overages.

Option B — Time‑boxed with Staged Invoices (simpler for finance)
- Structure: 6‑week timebox, access to specified models and endpoints, one midpoint invoice (30% at kickoff; 70% at midpoint).
- Surge handling: temporary grace window (48 hours) for traffic spikes; overage applies thereafter at pay‑as‑you‑go rate but with a 10% capped surcharge for the remainder of pilot.
- Billing: milestone invoices as requested.

Attachments: I’ve added a draft amendment with the credit lattice language and the procurement Qs filled in (redwood‑proposed‑amendment.docx). David, can you confirm the technical gating for the surge rule below? Kimberly, if legal needs clean language for the milestone invoice flow I’ll iterate.

Next step: Jordan — tell me which option procurement prefers and whether they require a DocuSign flow or a PO + SOW. If you want, we can schedule a 20‑minute call today to walk through exact numbers.

Thanks,

Quick technical note —

If NovaFluent chooses Option A (credit lattice) we should gate the surge grace on two metrics so we avoid stealthy load tests:
- Token spike duration < 48 hours (as Vanessa suggested)
- 99th percentile latency during spike remains within 1.5x baseline

Implementation: we can instrument a short webhook to notify NovaFluent and Redwood when a grace window is triggered; this allows automatic credit throttling if the conditions are not met. No infra changes required on your side.

Happy to demo the webhook behavior on a quick call.
